sections.label: SkillsFuture course fees and assessment
sections.summary: An MP asks whether SkillsFuture courses are assessed for cost and economic value, and the reply describes building progression pathways and lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) whether courses allowed under SkillsFuture are objectively assessed by the authorities as to how much they should cost and whether there is a negotiation process with training providers to keep course fees reasonable; and (b) whether there is an assessment of the courses to ensure that there are sufficient courses that can lead to tangible economic value-add for individuals rather than simply satisfying hobbies.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: It involves building up multiple pathways of progression, starting from schools and extending to our Post-secondary Education Institutes (PSEIs); developing new ways of education and training, including blended learning, extended internships and cooperation with industries; scaling up lifelong learning opportunities by expanding course offerings at every stage of a person's life.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: We are also planning on a major outreach programme called SkillsFuture Engage.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit course approval process
sections.summary: SSG examines proposed course fees using industry benchmarks and funding caps, and assesses courses as skills-based and industry-relevant, though some training may not relate to careers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: Nonetheless, as part of the approval process to include a course under SkillsFuture Credit, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) examines proposed course fees, using industry benchmarks and funding caps to ensure that they are reasonable relative to other similar courses.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: SSG, together with various supporting public agencies, also assess that SkillsFuture Credit courses are skills-based and relevant to industry or an individual's professional development.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: Many of these courses, such as those offered under the Singapore Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) framework, go through a structured and rigorous industry-validation process.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
sentences.text: But given that we take a deliberately inclusive approach for courses under SkillsFuture Credit in view of its promotional objective, and we reach out to all Singaporeans − young, mature, retired − it is inevitable that some Singaporeans will go for training not related to their careers.

sections.label: Top SkillsFuture course categories
sections.summary: The passage lists ten course categories, including information and communications, food and beverages, language skills, and business management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: The first was information and communications; second, food and beverages, third, language skills; fourth, service excellence; fifth, security and investigation; sixth, personal development; seventh, productivity and innovation; eighth, advertising, sales and marketing; ninth, leadership and people management; tenth, business management.

sections.label: Course costs and government subsidies
sections.summary: One data analytics course among the top eight costs $1,326, and many courses are highly subsidised by the Government to keep them affordable and accessible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Of the top eight courses that I had mentioned, one data analytics course costs $1,326.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to thank Ms Sun for her supplementary question.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: I want to assure her and Members that many of the courses are already highly subsidised by the Government to ensure that education and training courses are affordable and accessible.
